latin: Tota libertas est in ratione essentialiter.
translation: The whole of liberty is essentially in reason.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch3, from Latin at farmer1998:11662
doctrine: The thesis locates freedom essentially in reason rather than in will, a claim Edelheit calls 'not an obvious statement' since freedom is usually associated with the will rather than with reason or intellect (edelheit2022:11936). Farmer records no note of his own on this thesis.
context: Edelheit reads the thesis as returning, after the intervening thesis on Aristotelian physics, to the intellect-will debate already raised at thesis 2.19 (edelheit2022:11936).
historiography: Edelheit is the only scholar found discussing this thesis in the sources consulted; he flags it as a substantive, non-obvious philosophical claim rather than commenting on its reception (edelheit2022:11936).

quotations.text: Thesis 28 takes us away from Aristotelian physics and, similarly to thesis 19, back to the intellect-will debate.
It states that the whole of liberty consists essentially in reason.

not_established: The specific Thomistic text behind this thesis: not identified in the excerpt consulted (Farmer records no note of his own on it).
No reception, commission, or trial-related discussion of this thesis was found in the sources consulted.
